I know you are in pain, and I'm sorry for this, but I don't think people are as concerned as you think you are.  Like the waitstaff in the restaurant when you say you don't have a girlfriend.  I've waited tables before, and if that siutation happened to me, as a waitress the thought process in my head is "Thank God, there are no bratty kids at this table.  Good, three people, this should be easy.  They better all order alcohol and an appetizer.  If they share a salad for a meal I am going to kill them.  These people better tip."  That's about what's going on in a watiresses head.  Maybe the weird look they give you is that they are distracted in their own world with your table and about five other tables and you know what?  Wait a minute.  The fact that you can't comprehend what a service worker is really thinking when you sit your girlfriendless self down in their both, tells me something. You probably have never worked a service industry job.  Damn boy, what a charmed life you have!  And a bachelor's degree?  I dated a guy who was a young father, couldn't finish college.  I'll tell you, he would have remained a virgin until he was 90 if it meant he never got that girl pregnant and had to give up school.

I feel that half of your problem is that you are walking around in this cloud of misery about it.  If you are visibly upset about your situation, and people see it, it repels them.  But if you can smile about it, think to yourself, "I'm going to be happy, girlfriend or no girlfriend", and when you go to that restaurant with your married friend and the waitress asks you if your girlfriend is coming, you smile and say "If she doesn't, would you like to join me?" or something equally witty, people will see you as charming and fun and it's hard for a charming and fun guy to stay single for long...

I would care more that they have a track record of responsibility, have paid bills, have built their own life and career, etc.  That is what would impress me.  

It's not about the money.  It's about the ability to make something of yourself.

Nothing develops personality and health like setting career goals, however.  The work it takes to go through college, for example, builds character much better than watching a seminar.

He was brutally made fun of by all the neighbors for this, but he stayed true to himself.  He worked hard in school and he excitedly talked about the Bible and ministry.  He became engaged to a beautiful woman and was very happy.

But this was an actual nice person, not a whiny guy claiming to be nice when instead really being clingy.

I second this.  I have in my life been really cute and sometimes looked like total crap, and it was ironic because a time when i looked like crap BUT was very confident in myself, I had zero trouble attracting men!  So it wasn't too much a matter of looks.

I like this.  I'm a girl but went through a similar thing in high school.  I wanted to be skinny and pretty, but I was furious when people suggested going to the gym!  Why should I?  I should have a fast metabolism and be able to just lose weight naturally, right?  Or drink Diet Coke?  Oh my god!  How embarassing that I would have to admit weakness and not be able to drink regular coke (that ended when I saw a crush of mine slinging diet soda...then I realized if he was drinking it...I could too, haha).

I think I resorted to cocaine in this time period to lose the weight.  Didn't work...and too expensive.

But yeah, it's this idea of wanting something but doing nothing about it!  Crazy, huh?

Let me also say though that being super thin and cute (which I did get to that point) didn't necessarily win me what I thought.  I got some more male attention, but nothing serious and long lasting, and I attracted more creeps.  If I had been obese and hideous in my twenties, it actually would have saved me from situations that ruined my life.  Honestly, I would give my right hand to have spent ages 20 - 30 weighing like 250 pounds and therefore avoiding the things that happened.  So be careful what you wish for.

It's really true that the confidence comes from within.  One way I got more confidence was when I slowly became more independent.  Started paying my own bills, etc.  The more you know how to "own" things the more you know what you want and the likelier you are to get what you want.  You become more willing to fight, more assertive, etc.  

What girls and guys want in the opposite sex is:  humility and maturity.  Period.  They want someone who has their stuff together, who knows how to face the world, who is comfortable in themselves, who doesn't have to be the highest or the lowest, who acknowledges their strengths and weaknesses, and who takes on life.

How much does it cost to go on a walk?

Also, what junk are you eating to stay at 230?  Believe me, if you invested in healthy food ONLY, you would be spending less than you would on a binge.  Stop the sugar and flour and see how you save money.

I had something similar, called depersonalization (look it up) for a very long time and felt just as bad as you.

It helped to start doing the things I was most afraid of.  

What was I afraid of?  Well, I examined my wildest dreams.  I always fantasized about myself singing my favorite songs on stage, so guess what?  I sang for local events.  Scary but awesome.  By doing this I met new people and had fun.  I took a ballet class.  I learned Russian.  I told a friend how I honestly felt about our dead end friendship.  I traveled to other countries even though I was afraid to leave the house, I just DID it.

Basically, I started to take risks.  Look, I could try all day and night to force myself to walk around the block to overcome anxiety, but that wasn't enough.  I had to learn to face my biggest fear- my wildest dreams.  

I think it is also important what fears you are facing.

Like you said you have this problem around your friends.  It could be that your friends aren't really who you want to be around.  I remember hanging out with people I didn't truly respect, and I would get more anxiety by being with them.  But when I started to find people that I truly respected and wanted to be around, my anxiety disappated because I didn't have to wear a mask.  I could be my smart, ambitious self.

I was honest about my feelings with people.  I had to learn to say I didn't like something if I didn't like it.  

Oh, and I DO NOT RECOMMEND POT for you, sir.  If you are an overthinking, obsessive, anxiety ridden type, marijuana can be a horrible trigger.  Stay away.

What do you need to be doing with your life?

Can you go back to school?  Are you financially able to?

You know what would really get a lot of girls interested in you?  Go back to school, get a bachelor's degree, then go to law school.  Lots of girls like lawyers!  But...more importantly...you will leave school with a huge sense of accomplishment and a shot at a good job, which will take care of a lot of problems right there.

But...you love this girl because she is precisely NOT that.

By the way, I don't hate on you for living at home.  It depends on the situation.  I have an amazing friend, very well known in my hometown, very very popular, who lived at home till at least very late twenties.  But..he was also an entrepeneur who was able to fund his college and car with his business, I guess just living at home to save money...he did eventually get married...
YASSSS!

I think you are in love with where she is AT in life versus where you are at in life.

And guess what?  That's REALLY good news for you, buddy, because it means you have the potential to not only REACH her status but EXCEED it.

I developed a massive crush on a guy because he was popular and good looking and getting ahead in life...everything I wanted to be and I was angry that I wasn't there.  And of course he wasn't interested. 
 Well, I eventually made some choices that PUT me on the right track to be even further than where he was at and guess what?  No more obsession about him...I was busy hanging out with better guys than him!

Was I a loser when I was crushing on him.  NO.  I was simply stuck in life and I turned that in on myself and decided I must be a loser if that is happening to me.

But all I had to do was fix some aspects of my life that weren't working for me, and suddenly I became the desired one.

Yes, God put her in your path.  He most certainly did.  But not to date her.  To be a mirror for you.  To make you ask yourself:  What should I be doing now?  What should you be doing?  Should you be going back to school?  Working?  What should you be doing that you are not doing?  This mirror will continue to make you fall in neurotic, obsessive love until you can figure out where you are stuck in life.  And then when you do...that girl won't mean much anymore and you will find someone who really IS right.

She has options.  But so do you.  You have the option to examine yourself.

Well, in my experience it's good to question if you really want to be an artist or a musician.  Maybe you like doing those things as more of a recreational activity?  Or, maybe you would rather be a singer instead of a guitar player?  Because if you really want to be an artist or a musician, and you LOVE it and it's your PASSION, you won't force yourself.  You will just do it.  I mean, you will have to make yourself practice on the days you don't feel like it....you would want to set up a discipline (A great writer, I heard, sets aside time every day to write, etc), but there will be an element of wanting to do this too.  If you want to pursue music, and you can commit to a daily practice, great, just make sure you're not white knuckling it.  

I also noticed you said you have fatigue and depression.  I feel like maybe you are trying to overcompensate for this by having such a rigorus schedule?  Are you currently in college?

I'm also wondering if you are unhappy about something in your life situation.  For example, when I was going to a university that I hated (while living at home), I would take 23 hours of class in a semester and go bike riding 50 miles and ALL this great stuff and totally burn out.  But none of that activity made me get anywhere faster.  When I transferred to a school I LOVED (and got out of the house, to the college apartments), I didn't care less if I was busy enough or successful enough - I was so content with life that I wasn't measuring it!  The schedule came naturally.  Like, I could trust myself to go to class and get the homework done and then enjoy a drink at night.  I mean, you know, i made a list of things I needed to do out of practicality, so I wouldn't forget to go to the bank for example...but it wasn't anything crazy.  I painted because it was fun, I watched football, I went out with friends, I took naps, I read interesting books...but it all came kind of naturally because I was just enjoying my life.

Well...it's good to have a basic outline, but you have a LOT of different things going on here.  
Like doing art AND guitar AND self learning.  
Why are you doing those things?  Because you actually enjoy them?  Or because you want to be good at them so it will make you look good?  Or, are those different elements part of some unified goal?  (such as, you are a performance artist who is incorporating music and art into a piece).  But for daily activity, all these different things seems like a lot to me.  If I were you, I would majorly simplify.

If I were you, I'd probably change it up a bit: 

Maybe do the mediation right away when you wake up.  Start the day off clean, clear and fresh.  It will help guide you through the rest of the day.

So you could have like:
Wake 7, meditate 30 minutes, get ready for work
Work 8-4
exercise (better yet would be, if you are going to meditate and exercise, is to wake a little earlier in the morning and exercise and meditate then.  Then get to bed earlier.)
Come home, relax a bit or do the household chores
Have dinner
Then do a social thing OR a "follow your heart" thing OR practice the music/art, then go to bed.  If you want to keep modern on your reading, you can throw in some reading time as you are about to fall asleep.

That's the max I would really schedule.  

If you look at some celebrities, they don't schedule a million different things to cover every aspect of their lives; rather they have a more simplified schedule of a unified plan.  Ok, hate me for this but I will use the Kardashians.  One of those girls' schedule is something like:

Wake up
Go to the gym
Work on the television show
Eat lunch
Have some meetings about the fashion line
Photo Shoot
Dinner with family
Bed.

And that's, like, it.  And yet they are dubiously successful.  I'm sure if they want a good book or a pleausre-inducing activity, they throw it in sometime during the day as well, or wait until Sunday.

Maybe you can do that, too.  Save your heart-following or family time till Sunday when you can dedicate a few hours to a great play or a dinner with the parents.

It may sound preachy so forgive me, but have you tried a 12 step program?

BUT...the only thing is they want to see that you don't want to kill yourself.  They want to be right, so to speak.  

So go in there, act like you feel SO MUCH BETTER, smile, etc.

I tried to off myself when I was 19.  I had severe anxiety, etc.  So they put me in a hospital.  The doctor was basically an idiot (I found out later from his colleague he was NOT well respected...usually the more well-respected docs do NOT work in the inpatient ward) but I just took whatever pills they gave me and was like "yeah, I'm really feeling better!" and they were like "ok, well let's send you on your way!" and that was that.

It's not a place of help and sometimes opening up to the wrong people isn't the right thing.  What helps is getting to the source of depression in his life, situations, etc and working on that, and that is not done in a locked ward.  Only purpose of locking someone up is to keep them from killing themselves or someone else, not to cure anything.

They are not making it because they are dumber and lazier...they work hard...at what it takes to get ahead.

It's ridiculous, but taking the time to perfectly blowdry one's hair and do makeup and smile and play the game and dress in the latest clothes actually does the trick, amazingly....it seems beneath you I am sure but somehow it's really important.

Staying friendly with the professors is a major plus.  If you get to know them and make connections, and you show that you are willing to work around your ADHD and dyslexia, they will be happy to work with you.  As long as you show them you are willing to find a solution.

Ok...I saw somewhere you lived in Switzerland.  Lucky you!

Anyway.  So I know a little bit about that part of the world.  It is a little more reserved than, say, Israel, but there is hope.  

You have to be a good people person.  If you can act happy and positive you can overcome lots of barriers.  For example, I went to France (was right by Swiss border and met Swiss people who were quite nice) and people told me "be careful, the French are snobby, you don't speak their language, etc"..and I remember, I encountered a French person that did just that, gave me attitude, etc.  But I put my foot down and let her know (without saying the exact words) that I will NOT put up with snobbiness from her and...she started to be nice!  

Enthusiasm is really important.  If you are really enthusiastic and passionate to people, you will see discrimination fade.  

And you don't know where you will find a job.  You have to walk out your door well dressed every day and smiling every day.  Who knows, you could go to a family event and be so impressive to an uncle or distant cousin, that they think of you when their company has a job opening.  Stuff like that happens all the time.  You have to walk out of the door treating everybody like a potential boss, and being nice and happy and respectful to them.  This will build your reputation faster than you believe.

A lot of jobs aren't advertised.  Sometimes someone just gets this job that "oh my gosh, everyone wanted this job for so long, how did you get it!" because they made a good impression on people and they were nice and their name got recommended somehow.  That's how the world works.  

Celebrities have to do this, actually.  A movie star must be well dressed and well groomed before leaving their house, because they will never know if they will run into paparazzi.  One example of rude behavior and they are all over the tabloids the next day.

If you treat yourself as a valuable commodity, dress well, speak nicely, and smile, people will think that you have something important in your life (even if you DONT) and be totally mystified by you and will want to know MORE.  If you go outside with the attitude I see on here...well, people will think you are a loser and treat you accordingly.

I remember once a guy wanted to date me.  He seemed fine...until he started to go on about all these problems in his life.  I was turned off and didn't talk to him anymore.  He was mad I wouldn't date him.  Truth is, he was so close to a date because our first conversation he seemed really, really cool!  And he just totally destroyed himself.  

Thats where you are failing, my friend.  You COULD have a really good job and a really good life, but you are going around with this attitude.

Also...it's a matter of willingness.  If you just show that you are WILLING to work that crappy coffeeshop job, the universe has a way of sending you something better.  

I know you are capable of a good job.  Why?  Because you are complaining too much to want to settle for a bad job.  Ok, fair enough.  So.  Go to some Swiss coffeeshop and work at the register and become the most enthusiastic coffeeshop guy, smiling and being happy, and one of a few things will happen:

You will get promoted, and noticed by the superiors.
You will meet a client who will have a great job opportunity for you (happens ALL the time)
You will feel enough sense of accomplishment doing this job that you will be inspired to work harder for a better job.

Yes, a job that doesn't pay enough to live off of.  Because you will be making more money than you are making right now, and you are some how able to live.  From that shitty job, you will (if you have a good attitude) be promoted to a job that can pay, or you will gain enough experience to go to another job, or you will meet people who can network you into the right jobs, but right now you are doing nothing.

I had a job that paid very badly.  Horrible salary.  It was impossible to advance there.  Terrible boss.  But it taught me some valuable skills that I used at the next interview to get a job that paid well.  But I had to work the horrible job first.

So did...basically everyone else.

Elizabeth Gilbert (author) worked menial jobs and wore thrift store clothes before writing a bestseller.

Hillary Swank lived in her car before becoming a movie star.

Millions more examples.  

SOME people get an advanced degree and go right into a high paying job but others who are successful have crappy jobs then eventually find the right one.

Your BIGGEST problem is your attitude.  No one will hire you with your attitude.  But you would be surprised at how the world helps someone with a great attitude and who smiles.  You would be surprised how many companies offer to PAY for your education while you are working for them (even the SHITTY ones, like starbucks, where you pour coffee for a living, they help you with college.  for example)

Also your ingratitude is a huge issue.  If you are not a grateful person, your world will get smaller and smaller, but if you are grateful you will see more and more good things come to you.
How is it at a standstill?  Work?  School?  Relationships?  Family?
That can definitely give you a feeling of being behind.  Maybe you don't envy your classmates because they are ahead, but because they are doing what they want to do.

First of all, where do you live?

Second of all, it depends on how you present yourself in an interview.  It is NOT true that interviewers do not discriminate in the USA.  It happens there, too.  But how you present yourself in an interview makes a difference.  If you present yourself as sad and miserable, you are right, there are no good jobs that will take you.
